surface_summary: Sir Alan Hume-Frazer is found murdered at Beechcroft Hall, with suspicion falling on his cousin David Hume-Frazer, who is tried and acquitted. A complex web of family secrets, blackmail, and multiple suspects including an Italian husband and a mysterious Japanese man complicate the case.
accepted_facts: Sir Alan Hume-Frazer was murdered with a Japanese Ko-Katana sword
David Hume-Frazer was found asleep in the library at the time of the murder
A drawer in Sir Alan's writing desk was forcibly opened and documents stolen
A mysterious Japanese man named Ooma was seen near Beechcroft and is linked to the crime
inferred_conclusions: David Hume-Frazer was the murderer due to opportunity and motive
Giovanni Capella killed Sir Alan out of jealousy and financial gain
Numagawa Jiro was complicit in the murder as an accomplice
mechanism_description: Mr. Ooma, a Japanese descendant of the original David Hume, committed the murder of Sir Alan Hume-Frazer to obtain incriminating family documents that could be used for blackmail. He used the Ko-Katana sword to kill Sir Alan after forcing open the drawer to steal the papers. Later, Ooma also killed Giovanni Capella to prevent interference. Ooma was ultimately confronted and died after injecting himself with snake poison during his arrest.
delivery_path: Ooma arrives at Beechcroft and observes the household
He forces open the writing-desk drawer to steal documents
Sir Alan confronts Ooma, who kills him with the Ko-Katana
Ooma attempts to kill David and Robert Hume-Frazer to cover his tracks
Ooma kills Giovanni Capella during a train journey
Ooma is tracked and confronted at Beechcroft by Brett and allies
Ooma injects himself with snake poison and dies after confession
outcome_result: Mr. Ooma is identified as the murderer and dies from self-administered poison after being captured.

false_assumption.statement: David Hume-Frazer was guilty of murdering his cousin Sir Alan.
false_assumption.why_it_seems_reasonable: David was found asleep in the library at the time of the murder and had a known family dispute with Sir Alan. Witnesses and circumstantial evidence pointed to him.
false_assumption.what_it_hides: The existence of a third man, Ooma, who resembled David and committed the murder while David was asleep.

supporting_points: David was found asleep in the library at the time of the murder
The stolen documents were missing while David was alone in the room
Witnesses saw a man resembling David near the crime scene
David had a motive related to family disputes and inheritance
false_solution.the_one_flaw: David had a solid alibi of being asleep and was unaware of the murder until after it happened

red_herrings.description: Giovanni Capella, the Italian husband of Margaret, is suspected due to his hostile behavior and possible financial motives.
red_herrings.points_at_suspect: Giovanni's quarrel with Margaret and his passion for Helen Layton
red_herrings.innocent_explanation: He was away in Naples at the time of the murder and later killed by Ooma.

red_herrings.description: Numagawa Jiro, a Japanese man, is suspected due to his connection with the Ko-Katana and involvement in typewritten letters.
red_herrings.points_at_suspect: His knowledge of the sword and suspicious behavior with his wife
red_herrings.innocent_explanation: He was an unwitting tool of Ooma and acted under duress.

closed_circle.rationale: All key suspects are family members or closely connected persons present in the locality with access to the crime scene and motive, forming a closed circle.

discriminating_test.design: A controlled confrontation at Beechcroft is arranged where Ooma is cornered in the library. The room is secured, and Ooma is challenged to surrender. The presence of the hypodermic syringe and the Ko-Katana sword are confirmed. The suspects are observed for reactions and attempts to escape or attack.
discriminating_test.knowledge_revealed: This test reveals Ooma's identity as the murderer through his possession of the murder weapon and his violent reaction. It also confirms his intent to kill the cousins and his use of poison.
discriminating_test.pass_condition: The suspect is caught in possession of the murder weapon and cannot escape or resist arrest without revealing guilt.

fair_play_explanation: The reader is given detailed descriptions of all key characters, their movements, and the timeline of events. Witness statements, physical evidence like the broken drawer and the Ko-Katana sword, and the anonymous typewritten letters are presented. The presence of a third man resembling the accused is hinted at early, and the significance of the Japanese motto and cultural details is explained. Careful attention to alibis and contradictions allows the reader to deduce the existence of Ooma as the true culprit.
